reply.text:
"The burn" is a fine signal that you're working hard, but it isn't what drives growth. Close-to-failure sets are, and high reps can get you there when the weight is right. For most lifts I'd run a mix: heavier work in the 5 to 8 range for the main lifts, then higher reps of 12 to 20 on isolation and machine work, where it's easy on the joints and easy to recover from.

Do you want more high-rep work added to your current program, or a rebuilt session around it? Tell me which lift or muscle group you mean, and I'll set it up.
